note: surface_gravity_derived_ms2, escape_velocity_derived_kms, light_time_*_s and orbit_check are derived by the plan author (GM/R^2 etc.). Every other numeric field cites sources[...]. Fields marked UNVERIFIED have no NASA source in this snapshot. Horizons ranges are sampled min/max over a 30-year window at 10-day step.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.solar_irradiance_basis: NSSDC fact sheet single printed value (no perihelion/aphelion split on page)

earth_range_km.basis: JPL Horizons OBSERVER table, geocentric (500@399) range, 2026-11-05 to 2056-11-05, 10-day step; min/max of samples (true extremes can lie slightly outside)

bodies.rotation_notes: Sidereal rotation 1407.6 h; solar day 4222.6 h (fact sheet). Orbital period 87.969 d.

hazards.thermal: Mean surface 440 K; 590-725 K on sunward side (fact sheet). Irradiance ~6.7x Earth (derived).
hazards.atmosphere: Surface-bounded exosphere, ~5e-15 bar; no drag (fact sheet).

orbit_altitude_km.basis: GAME ASSUMPTION for the circular range. Real reference: MESSENGER 200 km periapsis x 15,193 km apoapsis (altitude), 80 deg, 12 h (NSSDCA); later lowered to ~25 km (NASA Science MESSENGER page).

orbit_altitude_km.note: Reference orbit is real; circular min/max is a game assumption

orbit_check.note: Circular two-body period and central cylindrical-shadow minutes using the same formulas as dist/data/catalog.js (orbitPeriodMinutes, shadowMinutes). Derived by plan author, not a source value.

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.surface_gravity_note: Fact sheet prints mean 9.820; CODATA 2018 standard gravity 9.80665 (fact sheet note).

earth_range_km.basis: Not applicable: spacecraft in Earth orbit. Use ground-station slant range and relay (TDRS) in the comm model; deep-space signal delay ~0.

hazards.atmosphere: Surface pressure 1014 mb, scale height 8.5 km (fact sheet); drag decays low orbits.
hazards.radiation: Van Allen belts: unverified (no NASA figure fetched).

orbit_altitude_km.basis: GAME ASSUMPTION. Real references: Landsat 9 705 km / 98.2 deg / 99 min (USGS FS 2019-3008), PACE 676.5 km / 98 deg / 13:00 LTAN (NTRS 20190030760).

orbit_check.note: Circular two-body period and central cylindrical-shadow minutes using the same formulas as dist/data/catalog.js (orbitPeriodMinutes, shadowMinutes). Derived by plan author, not a source value.

bodies.name: Moon

heliocentric_distance_au.note: Orbits Earth at 384,400 km semimajor axis (fact sheet / SSD elements)

bodies.solar_irradiance_basis: NSSDC Moon fact sheet (Earth solar constant)

earth_range_km.basis: JPL Horizons geocentric range 2026-11-05..2056-11-05, 10-day step (sampled). Fact sheet mean perigee/apogee 363,300 / 405,500 km are what dist/data/nasa.js already uses.

bodies.rotation_notes: Sidereal 655.720 h, synodic month 29.53 d, tidally locked (fact sheet).

hazards.thermal: Equatorial diurnal range 95 K to 390 K (fact sheet).
hazards.radiation: Solar particle events apply; no body-specific figure fetched. See DONKI summary in NASA_DATA_PLAN.md.
hazards.gravity_field: Mascons make low circular orbits unstable (GRAIL results, NASA Science GRAIL page).

orbit_altitude_km.basis: Existing game range. Real references: LRO ~30 x 180 km science phase / 30-70 km exploration phase (NSSDCA); GRAIL ~55 km (JPL) / 50 km (NSSDCA).

orbit_check.note: Circular two-body period and central cylindrical-shadow minutes using the same formulas as dist/data/catalog.js (orbitPeriodMinutes, shadowMinutes). Derived by plan author, not a source value.

earth_range_km.basis: JPL Horizons OBSERVER table, geocentric (500@399) range, 2026-11-05 to 2056-11-05, 10-day step; min/max of samples (true extremes can lie slightly outside)

bodies.earth_range_note: Game currently uses 54.6e6..400.2e6 (NASA relay page). Fact sheet prints 54.6e6..401.4e6 (all-time bounds); Horizons 30-yr window 56.2e6..400.1e6.

hazards.atmosphere: 6.36 mb mean surface pressure (4.0-8.7 seasonal), scale height 11 km (fact sheet). Drag matters near ~125-150 km (MAVEN deep dip / periapsis).

hazards.thermal: Mean ~214 K; Viking 1 diurnal 184-242 K (fact sheet).

orbit_altitude_km.basis: Existing game range. Real references: MRO 255 x 320 km (NASA Facts), Odyssey ~400 x 400 km (NSSDCA), MAVEN 150 km periapsis with deep dips to ~125 km (NASA Facts / NSSDCA).

orbit_check.note: Circular two-body period and central cylindrical-shadow minutes using the same formulas as dist/data/catalog.js (orbitPeriodMinutes, shadowMinutes). Derived by plan author, not a source value.

bodies.name: Phobos
bodies.surface_gravity_note: No NASA printed value fetched; derived value below.

earth_range_km.basis: JPL Horizons OBSERVER table, geocentric (500@399) range, 2026-11-05 to 2056-11-05, 10-day step; min/max of samples (true extremes can lie slightly outside)

bodies.rotation_notes: Shape 27 x 22 x 18 km. Orbits Mars about three times a day; nearing Mars 1.8 m per century (NASA Science Phobos page).

hazards.gravity: Mars perturbation and irregular shape make Keplerian circular orbits a poor approximation (plan author reasoning, not a NASA quote).

orbit_altitude_km.basis: UNVERIFIED. No NASA orbiter has orbited Phobos; any game altitude is a pure assumption (prefer hover/proximity-ops or flyby mode).

bodies.name: Europa

earth_range_km.basis: JPL Horizons OBSERVER table, geocentric (500@399) range, 2026-11-05 to 2056-11-05, 10-day step; min/max of samples (true extremes can lie slightly outside)

bodies.rotation_notes: Rotation 85.2 h; mean temperature -170 C (Galilean satellite fact table).

hazards.radiation: Europa is bathed in radiation trapped in Jupiter magnetic field. Clipper electronics expect an average of a few thousand to tens of thousands of rads per flyby even with mitigation (JPL press kit); vault walls up to 9.2 mm Al-Zn.
hazards.power: Solar 50.26 W/m2 at Jupiter; Clipper arrays at least 700 W through prime mission; Juno about 400 W at Jupiter.

orbit_altitude_km.basis: Real: Clipper flyby altitude as low as 25 km, nearly 50 flybys (NASA Science). Orbiting Europa is not planned by NASA; maximum flyby altitude UNVERIFIED.

hazards.radiation: Inside Jupiter magnetosphere; NASA figure not fetched: unverified.

orbit_altitude_km.basis: UNVERIFIED. No NASA Ganymede orbiter in sources fetched; ESA JUICE is the orbiter (ESA source needed, not fetched).

bodies.name: Titan
bodies.surface_gravity_note: No NASA printed value fetched; derived below.

earth_range_km.basis: JPL Horizons OBSERVER table, geocentric (500@399) range, 2026-11-05 to 2056-11-05, 10-day step; min/max of samples (true extremes can lie slightly outside)

bodies.rotation_notes: Tidally locked, synchronous with Saturn; orbits Saturn in 15 d 22 h (NASA Science).

hazards.atmosphere: About 95% N2 and 5% CH4; surface pressure about 60% greater than Earth; surface -179 C (NASA Science Titan facts). Haze blocks visible imaging from orbit; Cassini used radar and IR.
hazards.power: 14.82 W/m2 at Saturn: RTG required (Cassini 885 W BOL).

orbit_altitude_km.basis: UNVERIFIED. Thick atmosphere; Cassini studied Titan via 127 targeted flybys (NASA Science), minimum flyby altitude not verified here. Dragonfly rotorcraft scheduled for 2028 launch (NASA Science).

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.surface_gravity_note: Fact sheet gives gravity at 1 bar; not used. Gas giant: no surface.

earth_range_km.basis: JPL Horizons OBSERVER table, geocentric (500@399) range, 2026-11-05 to 2056-11-05, 10-day step; min/max of samples (true extremes can lie slightly outside)

bodies.rotation_notes: Not fetched for this pass: unverified.

hazards.radiation: Dipole field 4.30 Gauss-Rj^3 tilted 9.4 deg; 1 Rj field 4.0-13.0 Gauss (GSFC-O6 model, fact sheet; Rj = 71,398 km). Juno titanium vault and Europa Clipper Al-Zn vault exist because of this. Absolute dose figures: unverified.
hazards.power: 50.26 W/m2: Juno 60 m2 arrays yield ~400 W (JPL press kit)

orbit_altitude_km.basis: Real: Juno perijove about 4,200 km above cloud tops, 14-day science orbit (NSSDCA); polar. Maximum UNVERIFIED (53.5-day capture orbit).

radius_km.note: 69,911 km volumetric mean; JPL phys_par identical

gm_km3s2.note: BODY599_GM Jupiter body only; system barycenter 126712764.1
